answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can require proof-of-staked-attestation: each agent must lock a non-trivial deposit before its votes count, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits. Reputation then grows like a vine along verified behavior rather than scattering like the plume of a dandelion, and a juniper-like slow-trust tree -- referrals maturing only over time -- makes mass-produced sockpuppets uneconomical, since attackers must risk real capital and wait real months.
